name: huhhb
description: Uhstray.io's curated Claude Code skills marketplace — workflows and automation for engineering teams.

skills.name: session-save
skills.description: Use when ending or pausing a session and you want to resume cleanly later — writes a gitignored continuation file (.claude/CONTINUE.md) with the exact next action, conversation context, and working-tree state.

skills.name: session-resume
skills.description: Use when picking up prior work in a fresh session — consumes the continuation file written by session-save: verifies it against the repo, re-hydrates context, briefs, deletes the file, then acts.

skills.name: memory
skills.description: Access, search, and manage the team memory nexus — powered by MemPalace. Store and recall project context via MCP.

skills.name: memory-search
skills.description: Semantic search across the team memory nexus.

skills.name: memory-mine
skills.description: Mine a project directory or text into the memory nexus.

skills.name: memory-status
skills.description: Show memory nexus statistics — drawer count, wings, rooms.

skills.name: repo-memory
skills.description: Save and retrieve project knowledge in .claude/memory/ — triggers on 'remember', 'don't forget', 'recall', 'what do we know about', and similar phrases.

skills.name: huhhb-welcome
skills.description: First-run tour of huhhb skills.

skills.name: huhhb-skills
skills.description: List all available huhhb skills.

skills.name: onboarding
skills.description: Use when setting up Claude Code for the first time, configuring auto mode, enabling agent teams, or when user says set up Claude or onboard me

skills.name: using-superpowers
skills.description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring Skill tool invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions

skills.name: brainstorming
skills.description: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.

skills.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skills.description: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies

skills.name: executing-plans
skills.description: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints

skills.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skills.description: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work - guides completion of development work by presenting structured options for merge, PR, or cleanup

skills.name: subagent-driven-development
skills.description: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

skills.name: using-git-worktrees
skills.description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - creates isolated git worktrees with smart directory selection and safety verification

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

skills.name: writing-plans
skills.description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code

skills.name: writing-skills
skills.description: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment

skills.name: receiving-code-review
skills.description: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation

skills.name: requesting-code-review
skills.description: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements

skills.name: training
skills.description: Socratic teaching mode (Sensei). Never writes new code — guides users through problems by describing approaches, naming APIs, linking docs, and asking questions that lead to the answer.

skills.name: caveman
skills.description: Ultra-compressed communication mode sourced from JuliusBrussee/caveman. Cuts token usage ~75% while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports lite, full, ultra, and wenyan intensity levels.

skills.name: caveman-commit
skills.description: Ultra-compressed commit message generator. Conventional Commits format, subject ≤50 chars, body only when why isn't obvious.

skills.name: caveman-review
skills.description: Ultra-compressed code review comments. One line per finding: location, problem, fix. No throat-clearing.

skills.name: caveman-compress
skills.description: Compress natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos) into caveman format to save input tokens. Preserves all technical substance.

skills.name: caveman-help
skills.description: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands.

skills.name: caveman-stats
skills.description: Real-time token usage metrics for the current session. Requires caveman plugin hooks to function — install via JuliusBrussee/caveman for full functionality.

skills.name: cavecrew
skills.description: Use when delegating code tasks to compressed subagents — investigator, builder, and reviewer — to preserve main context length.

skills.name: strict-simplify
skills.description: Replace redundant or verbose logic with a provably-equivalent simpler form, apply the edits, and show the diff. Strict: no restructuring, renaming, reformatting, optimizing, or bug-fixing.

skills.name: strict-refactor
skills.description: Decompose large functions into named single-purpose units — extract computation blocks, guard clauses, or setup phases, or move a function to a better module. Strict: verbatim extraction only, no logic changes, no renames.

skills.name: explaining-plans
skills.description: Use when augmenting or explaining a plan, spec, or RFC — enriches the document in place with decision criteria, cited source context, target-outcome framing, and prose-introduced mermaid diagrams. Composes with writing-plans rather than replacing it.

skills.name: explaining-changes
skills.description: Use during implementation to narrate changes as they happen — explains each logical change, each completed plan task, and every commit, using brief prose plus simple ASCII diagrams. Chat/CLI only.

skills.name: grounding
skills.description: Use when a long session should pause for a checkpoint — surfaces in-flight work, runs /simplify + /security-review and test/build/lint health, checks the diff against the repo's documented conventions, and re-confirms goals. Fired by the grounding hook (default 2h, configurable) or run manually. Opt-in; offers a user-selectable check menu.

skills.name: evolve
skills.description: Cross-session memory protocol backed by Honcho — how to recall what evolve has learned about you, persist durable facts, and route knowledge to the right memory stratum. Inert until configured.

skills.name: evolve-review
skills.description: The learning pass — triage captured session observations into overlay-skill patches, new overlays, or repo-memory entries, with diffs and approval; also approves proposals staged by headless runs.

skills.name: evolve-status
skills.description: Health check for the evolve learning loop — spool depth, deriver queue, cache age, overlay confidence table, pending proposals.

skills.name: evolve-skills
skills.description: The library lifecycle pass — audits every skill against usage telemetry, bench history, and lint debt; issues refine/merge/prune/create verdicts and distills new skills from proven successful sessions, eval-gated.

skills.name: evolve-distill
skills.description: Distill a repeated, successful multi-step workflow from past sessions into a reusable overlay skill — eval-gated, ≥2-session evidence, human-approved; stages a proposal, never writes a skill directly.

skills.name: evolve-map
skills.description: Inventory every skill across tiers (repo/user/plugin), draw the relationships between them (overlaps, complements, composes, supersedes, gaps), recommend augment-vs-build, avoid duplicates, and promote a user skill to the repository.
